History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
Adult female with 2-day history of progressively worsening constant burning lower abdominal pain and subjective fever; pink-tinged urine and urinary frequency; empirically treated today for probable urinary tract infection with trimethoprim and advised pregnancy test and safety-net follow-up.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Burning pain below umbilicus for 2 days, constant, gradually worsening.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Pink-tinged urine, ↑ urinary frequency.  
  – Mild nausea; no vomiting.  
  – Felt hot/sweaty; temperature not recorded.  
  – Bowels now normal after brief constipation last week; no diarrhea.  
  – No dysuria, no chest symptoms, no palpitations, headaches, or visual changes.  
• Gynecologic/sexual history:  
  – Sexually active with same partner; last intercourse 4 days ago.  
  – On Implanon (inserted 1 year ago); still menstruating.  
  – Last menstrual period “about three weeks ago” then corrected to “two weeks ago” (conflict noted).  
  – Last STD screen 6 months ago, normal.  
• Past episodes: No similar pain previously.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• No prior surgeries.

Medications:
• Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• New prescription: Trimethoprim 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days.  
• Advice to use paracetamol – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• Not documented.

Social History:
• Lives in share house with two roommates.  
• Occupation: Accountant.  
• Non-smoker.  
• Social alcohol use; no quantified intake.  
• No recreational drug use mentioned.

Family History:
• No known relevant family history.

Physical Examination:
• No in-person examination or vitals documented (teleconsult).

Investigations:
• None performed today.  
• Advised home urinary pregnancy test.  
• Clinician discussed need for further tests (e.g., urinalysis, other labs) if symptoms persist or worsen.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected urinary tract infection
  – Plan: Trimethoprim 1 tab BID x 3 days; increase oral fluids; consider cranberry juice.
  – Safety-net: Return or call if worsening abdominal pain, persistent fever, vomiting, or no improvement within a few days.

Issue 2: Possible pregnancy-related abdominal pain
  – Plan: Perform home pregnancy test; report result.

Issue 3: Abdominal pain of uncertain etiology (GI vs other)
  – Plan: Monitor symptoms; if no improvement, arrange further evaluation (urinalysis, blood work, imaging as indicated).

General Plan items:
• Analgesia: Paracetamol as needed.  
• Follow-up: Reassess in a few days or sooner if red-flag symptoms develop.  
• Prescription sent electronically to patient’s pharmacy.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: Allergies, comprehensive medication reconciliation, vitals, physical examination findings.  
• Internal conflicts: Patient addressed as “Tim” then “Kim”; last menstrual period stated as “three weeks ago” then “two weeks ago.”  
• Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor name discrepancy and conversational repetition noted.
